label: Thomas Aquinas, Sententia libri…: Things… supports If x depends for its being on y, then x…
note: In V Metaph. lect. 13 n. 18 states that priors can be without posteriors 'et non e converso': the posterior, which depends on the prior, cannot be without it. The premise states this for every x that depends for its being on y, with dependence in the counterfactual sense of DEF-DEPENDS-FOR-BEING; the passage speaks only of posteriors in the order of being and gives no analysis of dependence.
